Map Skills and Geographic Tools: Geography
The study of Earth's physical features and human activity across space
Latitude
Distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees
Longitude
Distance east or west of the prime meridian
Equator
The zero-degree line of latitude circling Earth's middle
Prime meridian
The zero-degree line of longitude running through Greenwich
Absolute location
An exact position given by coordinates
Relative location
A position described in relation to other places
Map scale
The ratio between distance on a map and distance on the ground
Map projection
A method of showing a curved Earth on a flat surface
Mercator projection
A projection preserving direction but badly distorting polar area
Robinson projection
A compromise projection balancing shape and area distortion
Topographic map
A map showing elevation with contour lines
Thematic map
A map displaying a single subject such as population or rainfall
Legend
The key explaining a map's symbols
GIS
Software layering geographic data for analysis
GPS
A satellite system providing precise positioning
Time zone
A region using the same standard clock time
International Date Line
The roughly 180-degree line where the calendar date changes

A natural feature of Earth's surface
Plate tectonics
The theory that Earth's lithosphere moves in large plates
Continental drift
The gradual movement of continents over geologic time
Fault
A fracture in rock along which movement occurs
Plateau
An elevated area of relatively flat land
Basin
A low area surrounded by higher land
Delta
A landform of deposited sediment at a river's mouth
Peninsula
Land surrounded by water on three sides
Isthmus
A narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses
Archipelago
A chain or cluster of islands
Strait
A narrow water passage connecting two larger bodies of water
Tributary
A smaller stream flowing into a larger river
Watershed
The land area draining into a particular river system
Erosion
The transport of weathered material by water, wind, or ice
Glacier
A slow-moving mass of ice that carves the landscape
Ring of Fire
The Pacific rim zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanoes

A large flow of seawater that redistributes heat

The warm Atlantic current that moderates western Europe

Savanna
Tropical grassland with distinct wet and dry seasons

Mediterranean climate
Mild wet winters with hot dry summers
Tundra
A cold treeless biome with permanently frozen subsoil

Ground that stays frozen for at least two consecutive years
Monsoon
A seasonal wind reversal bringing heavy summer rainfall

A large ecological region defined by climate and vegetation

A Pacific warming pattern that shifts weather worldwide
